source: Bantay-written Philippine facts. Common knowledge, no text copied from any site.
facts: General Santos is called the Tuna Capital of the Philippines.
The Philippines has more than 7,000 islands.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is known for its almost perfect cone shape.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird, and it is one of the biggest eagles in the world.
The Philippine tarsier is a tiny animal with huge eyes. It lives in Bohol and some other islands.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains about 2,000 years ago.
In the Philippines, Christmas songs start playing in September, when the Ber months begin.
The first jeepneys were made from army jeeps left behind after World War II.
The mango is the national fruit of the Philippines.
Sampaguita is the national flower. Many people string it into garlands.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are more than 1,200 round hills. The grass turns brown in the dry season.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River in Palawan runs through a cave to the sea.
Narra is the national tree of the Philippines.
Taal Volcano sits on an island inside a lake in Batangas.
Butanding is the Filipino name for the whale shark. People watch them in Donsol, Sorsogon.
Davao is famous for durian, and Mindanao grows much of the country's bananas and pineapples.
Filipino and English are the two official languages of the Philippines.
General Santos sits on Sarangani Bay in Mindanao.
A church in Las Pinas has a pipe organ made mostly of bamboo.
Halo-halo means mix-mix. It is a cold dessert of ice, milk and sweet toppings.
